# Byterygon UI registry

> Base UI components styled with Byterygon design-token roles, as a static shadcn registry. No network: install from this folder or from a static server you host.

[llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) has the same and, in full, every component's examples and the token catalogue (each role's purpose, CSS variable, Tailwind name and values per mode).

Install (components.json: "registries": { "@byterygon": "<this folder or URL>/{name}.json" }, "tailwind": { "baseColor": "" }):

    shadcn add <this folder>/theme-default.json @byterygon/button

Rules for code on these components (the ESLint and Stylelint rules of @byterygon/lint enforce them; their messages name the role to use):

- Style with the token roles only: Tailwind names such as bg-surface, text-fg-muted, border-border-subtle, p-inset-sm, gap-gap-md, h-control-md, rounded-md, text-body-1, shadow-layer. No raw colours (#hex, rgb(), oklch(), bg-blue-500), no arbitrary values (p-[13px]) other than token variables (var(--by-...)), no raw space steps (p-2, gap-3).
- Props follow Fluent 2: appearance (primary, secondary, outline, subtle, transparent; danger on Button and IconButton; outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter on fields) and size (small, medium, large). The old variant and sm/md/lg still work for one release and are marked deprecated below.
- Icons: the Icon component with an icon from @/lib/icons (Fluent UI System Icons, vendored), never an icon font or a CDN.
- Themes are files (seeds plus overrides): edit one, then run `by-tokens validate` (@byterygon/design-tokens); `by-tokens search <words>` and `by-tokens explain <token>` find and describe tokens.

## Themes

- [theme-default](theme-default.json): The Byterygon default, Aurora (Fluent 2 layered look): violet #6b4eff brand, cool grey neutral, violet and aqua glows behind translucent layers, radius 4 and 8, a black and white focus ring.
- [theme-classic](theme-classic.json): Classic: the Byterygon default before Fluent 2 (TSK-57): a blue-teal brand on a neutral tinted with the same hue, light by default, comfortable density, WCAG 2.2 AA, and the fonts it had (Inter, then JetBrains Mono).
- [theme-high-contrast](theme-high-contrast.json): High contrast: WCAG 2.2 AAA (7:1 text, 4.5:1 for controls and focus), pure grey neutral, a deep blue accent and a thick focus ring. Comfortable density.
- [theme-midnight](theme-midnight.json): Midnight: dark first, on a deep blue neutral with a periwinkle accent. The light scheme is a cool blue-tinted counterpart. Comfortable density.
- [theme-paper](theme-paper.json): Paper: a warm light theme for reading. Cream backgrounds, a rust accent (so its orange, the warning colour, leans to amber), larger text with relaxed line height, rounder corners, comfortable density.
- [theme-slate](theme-slate.json): Slate: near-greyscale and minimal. A muted slate-blue accent on a barely tinted neutral, square-ish corners, light by default, comfortable density.
- [theme-terminal](theme-terminal.json): Terminal: dark first, a green accent on a green-black neutral, monospace for all interface text, 13 px text, square corners, compact density.

## Components

### Accordion

[accordion.json](accordion.json): A stack of sections with heading triggers that open one at a time, or several with multiple; the panel fades in.

Usage: Use Accordion for a list of sections a user reads or edits one at a time: settings groups, FAQ-style help, the parts of a long connection form. Compose Accordion > AccordionItem (value) > AccordionTrigger + AccordionPanel. defaultValue and value are arrays of open values; multiple lets several stay open. For a single optional block use Collapsible; for views the user switches between, use Tabs.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/accordion
- Parts: AccordionItem (data-slot accordion-item): One section; value identifies it, disabled turns it off.; AccordionTrigger (data-slot accordion-trigger): The heading and toggle: an <h3> with a full-width button and a chevron.; AccordionPanel (data-slot accordion-panel): The section's content, shown while open.
- variant: plain, outline
- Props: variant ("plain" | "outline", default "plain"); value (unknown[]); defaultValue (unknown[]); onValueChange ((value: unknown[], details) => void); multiple (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); children (ReactNode); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: open (in-data-panel-open), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled), entering (data-starting-style), leaving (data-ending-style)
- Tokens: color.bg.layer, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.link, color.fg.muted, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.layer.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, opacity.disabled, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.icon.md, size.panel.md, space.inline.md, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight
- Accessibility: Each trigger is a <button> inside an <h3>, with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming its panel; Enter and Space toggle it. Triggers are native buttons in the tab order; Tab and Shift+Tab move between them. Base UI's Accordion has no arrow-key navigation between headers (optional in the ARIA accordion pattern). The panel is a region labelled by its trigger and is removed from the DOM while closed. The chevron is aria-hidden; the state is announced through aria-expanded. Its turn stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

### Alert

[alert.json](alert.json): A message in the page flow, in five tones with a status icon, a title, a description, actions and an optional close button; inline box or full-width banner.

Usage: Use Alert for a message that belongs to a place on the page and stays until the condition changes: a query error under the editor (with SQLSTATE in <code>), a plaintext warning in the connection form, a grant about to expire across the top (layout="banner"). Compose Alert > AlertTitle, AlertDescription, AlertActions. Render it when the condition occurs: danger and warning are role="alert" and are announced at once. For a transient confirmation use Toast; for a decision the user must make, AlertDialog; for an empty view, EmptyState. The old variant prop still works for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: AlertTitle (data-slot alert-title): The message in a few words.; AlertDescription (data-slot alert-description): What happened and what to do.; AlertActions (data-slot alert-actions): Buttons that act on the message.
- intent: neutral, info, success, warning, danger
- layout: inline, banner
- Props: intent ("neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", default "neutral"); variant ("neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", deprecated: use intent); layout ("inline" | "banner", default "inline"); icon (ReactNode | false); onDismiss (() => void); dismissLabel (string, default "\"Dismiss\""); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.bg.layer, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.info.bg, color.status.info.border, color.status.info.fg, color.status.success.bg, color.status.success.border, color.status.success.fg, color.status.warning.bg, color.status.warning.border, color.status.warning.fg, font.mono, font.sans, radius.md, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, space.inline.sm, space.inset.md, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: Danger and warning alerts are role="alert" (assertive), the others role="status" (polite). Insert the alert when the condition occurs so it is announced; one already on the page at load may not be. The icon is aria-hidden; the title and description say the status in words, not by colour alone. The close button is an IconButton named by dismissLabel; move focus to a sensible place after dismissing if it was inside the alert. Text colours are the status fg roles on the status subtle backgrounds, which the token build checks for contrast; long identifiers wrap.

### AlertDialog

[alert-dialog.json](alert-dialog.json): A decision the user must make before going on, on Base UI's AlertDialog: Dialog's scrim and popup with role="alertdialog", no close button and no dismissal by an outside click, a Cancel and an Action in the footer.

Usage: Use AlertDialog to confirm an action that destroys data or cannot be undone (delete a connection, run a destructive statement) or to approve something with consequences (grant access). Compose it as AlertDialog > AlertDialogTrigger (render a Button; or open it through open) + AlertDialogContent > AlertDialogHeader (AlertDialogTitle: the question or consequence; AlertDialogDescription), an optional AlertDialogBody (the statement, the target), AlertDialogFooter (AlertDialogCancel, then the action). An action that finishes at once can be an AlertDialogCancel with appearance="danger" (it closes); an action that waits for the core is an AlertDialogAction with loading, and the caller closes the dialog through open when it succeeds. Name the action after what it does ("Delete", "Approve and save"), not "OK". For a task that may be dismissed freely use Dialog.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/alert-dialog
- Parts: AlertDialogTrigger (data-slot alert-dialog-trigger): Opens the dialog; unstyled, render a Button through render.; AlertDialogContent (data-slot alert-dialog-content): The portal with the scrim, the viewport and the popup; no close button.; AlertDialogBackdrop (data-slot alert-dialog-backdrop): The scrim; AlertDialogContent renders it.; AlertDialogViewport (data-slot alert-dialog-viewport): The centring layer; AlertDialogContent renders it.; AlertDialogHeader (data-slot alert-dialog-header): The title and description, stacked.; AlertDialogTitle (data-slot alert-dialog-title): An <h2> in text.subtitle-1 (Fluent's dialog title) that names the dialog.; AlertDialogDescription (data-slot alert-dialog-description): A <p> in color.fg.muted that describes the dialog.; AlertDialogBody (data-slot alert-dialog-body): What the decision is about; scrolls when long.; AlertDialogFooter (data-slot alert-dialog-footer): Cancel, then the action, at the end of the row.; AlertDialogCancel (data-slot alert-dialog-cancel): A Button (ghost by default) that closes the dialog.; AlertDialogAction (data-slot alert-dialog-action): A Button (primary by default) that runs the action and does not close the dialog by itself.
- size: sm, md, lg, xl
- Props: size ("sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl", default "md"); open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); appearance ("primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "subtle" | "transparent" | "danger"); variant ("primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); loading (boolean, default false); initialFocus (RefObject<HTMLElement> | boolean); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style), loading (data-loading)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.scrim, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, color.status.danger.solid-hover, elevation.dialog.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.gentle, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.icon.lg, size.panel.lg, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inset.lg, space.inset.sm, space.stack.md, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, text.subtitle-1.leading, text.subtitle-1.size, text.subtitle-1.tracking, text.subtitle-1.weight, z.modal, z.overlay
- Accessibility: The popup is role="alertdialog", named by AlertDialogTitle and described by AlertDialogDescription; while it is open the rest of the page is inert and hidden from assistive technology. Opening moves focus to the first focusable element (Cancel in the usual footer order, so Enter does not confirm by accident); Tab stays inside; closing returns focus to the trigger. Escape closes it (as Cancel); a press outside does not. The action names what it does; a destructive one uses the danger appearance and its text, so the meaning does not rest on colour. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the scale and fade transitions off.

### Avatar

[avatar.json](avatar.json): A person's or a service's picture, with initials (or another fallback) while it loads or when there is none; circle or square in three sizes.

Usage: Use Avatar beside a name: the signed-in user, who approved a grant, a connection in a list (shape="square"). name is the accessible name and the source of the initials; src is a local or data: URL, never a remote service in an air-gapped app. fallback replaces the initials (an icon). The picture shows only once loaded. For a status next to a name use Badge.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/avatar
- size: sm, md, lg
- shape: circle, square
- Props: name (string); src (string); fallback (ReactNode); size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); shape ("circle" | "square", default "circle"); fallbackDelay (number); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLSpanElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, font.sans, radius.md, size.control.lg, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-2-strong.leading, text.caption-2-strong.size, text.caption-2-strong.tracking, text.caption-2-strong.weight
- Accessibility: The root is role="img" with aria-label from name; the picture has alt="" and the initials are aria-hidden, so the name is read once. When the avatar sits next to the same name in text, it repeats it; that is acceptable, or pass aria-hidden on the Avatar to skip it. Initials are color.neutral.subtle-fg on color.neutral.subtle-bg, contrast-checked by the token build. Not focusable.

### Badge

[badge.json](badge.json): A short, non-interactive label for status or a count, in six tones and four appearances, including a coloured dot before plain text.

Usage: Use Badge for a word or a number that describes something next to it: a connection's state (appearance="dot"), a grant's mode (read-only, plaintext), a count. variant picks the tone (neutral, accent, danger, warning, success, info), appearance the weight: subtle in lists, solid for what must stand out, outline on busy surfaces, dot for live state. Keep it to one or two words; the text must say the status, never the colour alone. For a removable or clickable label use Tag; for a column's data type use TypeBadge; for a message use Alert.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: neutral, accent, danger, warning, success, info
- appearance: subtle, tint, solid, outline, dot
- size: sm, md
- Props: variant ("neutral" | "accent" | "danger" | "warning" | "success" | "info", default "neutral"); appearance ("subtle" | "tint" | "solid" | "outline" | "dot", default "subtle"); size ("sm" | "md", default "sm"); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.compound, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-bg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.neutral.bg, color.neutral.fg, color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, color.status.info.bg, color.status.info.border, color.status.info.fg, color.status.info.solid, color.status.info.solid-fg, color.status.success.bg, color.status.success.border, color.status.success.fg, color.status.success.solid, color.status.success.solid-fg, color.status.warning.bg, color.status.warning.border, color.status.warning.fg, color.status.warning.solid, color.status.warning.solid-fg, font.sans, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.xs, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight
- Accessibility: A <span> of text, read in place; not focusable and not interactive. The status is in the words ("connected", "plaintext"); colour and the dot only repeat it, so nothing is conveyed by colour alone. The dot is aria-hidden. Solid and subtle text colours are the status solid-fg and fg roles, which the token build checks for contrast on their backgrounds. For a count, add context for screen readers when the number alone is ambiguous ("3 notices", or visually hidden text).

### Breadcrumb

[breadcrumb.json](breadcrumb.json): Where the user is in a hierarchy, as a trail of links: a <nav> with an ordered list of links, the current place, separators and an ellipsis for collapsed items, on Base UI's useRender; useBreadcrumbOverflow folds the first items into the ellipsis when the trail does not fit.

Usage: Use Breadcrumb to show and move up a path: connection, schema, table, column; a settings section. Compose it as Breadcrumb > BreadcrumbList > BreadcrumbItem (BreadcrumbLink with href, or render a router link) with BreadcrumbSeparator between items, and BreadcrumbPage for the last, current place. Collapse a long middle into BreadcrumbEllipsis inside a DropdownMenuTrigger listing the hidden places. It is not a substitute for navigation: use Sidebar or NavigationMenu for that; for steps of a task, Stepper. When the trail can be longer than its room, useBreadcrumbOverflow({ count, signature, available? }) gives the list ref and the indexes to fold: mark each BreadcrumbItem with data-breadcrumb-index={i} and the ellipsis item with data-breadcrumb-overflow, and render one ellipsis menu in place of the folded items; the last two always show (Fluent's rule).

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: BreadcrumbList (data-slot breadcrumb-list): An <ol> that wraps on narrow widths, in color.fg.muted.; BreadcrumbItem (data-slot breadcrumb-item): An <li> holding a link, the page or an ellipsis.; BreadcrumbLink (data-slot breadcrumb-link): An <a> (or render) in color.fg.muted, underlined and color.fg.default on hover, truncated when long.; BreadcrumbPage (data-slot breadcrumb-page): The current place, a <span> with aria-current="page" in color.fg.default.; BreadcrumbSeparator (data-slot breadcrumb-separator): An aria-hidden <li> with a chevron or the given mark, in color.fg.subtle.; BreadcrumbEllipsis (data-slot breadcrumb-ellipsis): Three dots for collapsed places, with visually hidden text "More places".
- Props: aria-label (string, default "Breadcrumb"); href (string); render (ReactElement | (props) => ReactElement); children (ReactNode); className (string); data-breadcrumb-index (number); data-breadcrumb-overflow (string)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, space.inline.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight
- Accessibility: The trail is a <nav> landmark named "Breadcrumb" holding an ordered list, so its length and order are announced. The current place has aria-current="page" and is not a link; the separators are aria-hidden, so they are not read between items. Links are in the tab order with a visible focus ring; a collapsed middle is a menu button with an accessible name. Long names are truncated visually but keep their full text for assistive technology. Only colours transition; nothing moves. Folded places stay reachable: the ellipsis is a menu button listing them, and the current place and its parent never fold.

### Button

[button.json](button.json): Fluent 2's Button: primary, secondary, outline, subtle and transparent appearances (plus Byterygon's danger) in small, medium and large, with hover, pressed, focus (the double ring), disabled and loading states.

Usage: Use one primary Button per view for the main action, secondary for the others, outline where an edge without a fill reads better, subtle in toolbars and dense rows, transparent for a link-like action, danger for one that destroys data. Medium is the default size; small in dense rows, large for a main call to action. Give it a visible text label (an Icon from @/lib/icons may go before it); for an icon alone use IconButton. Set loading while the action runs instead of disabling it, and type="submit" inside a form. The old variant prop (ghost is subtle) and the sm/md/lg sizes still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/button
- appearance: primary, secondary, outline, subtle, transparent, danger
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: appearance ("primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "subtle" | "transparent" | "danger", default "primary"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); variant ("primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); loading (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); type ("button" | "submit" | "reset", default "button"); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: hover (hover), active (active), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled), loading (data-loading)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.default, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, color.status.danger.solid-hover, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.sm, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight
- Accessibility: Renders a native <button> with type="button" unless type is set, so Enter and Space activate it. An icon-only button needs aria-label (use IconButton, whose type requires it). Disabled uses the native disabled attribute; loading keeps the button focusable (aria-disabled) so focus is not lost mid-action, and sets aria-busy. The focus ring shows for keyboard focus only (focus-visible): an outline in color.ring, which forced-colours mode keeps, around an inner stroke in color.ring-inner; color.ring meets 3:1 on every surface and layer (token pairs). Text and fill pairs of every appearance are contrast-checked by the token build in light and dark; disabled text is exempt (WCAG 1.4.3).

### Calendar

[calendar.json](calendar.json): A month grid to pick one day, several days or a range, on react-day-picker with date-fns, styled with token roles: control-sized day buttons, the accent solid for the chosen day and the accent subtle band for a range.

Usage: Use Calendar on its own where the month should stay visible (a history window, a schedule), or let DatePicker open it in a popup next to a text field. Set mode to "single", "multiple" or "range" and pass selected and onSelect as react-day-picker's (Date, Date[] or { from, to }). Limit the choice with disabled matchers ({ before }, { after }, a weekday list), show two months for ranges with numberOfMonths={2}, and pass a date-fns locale for the language and the first day of the week (weekStartsOn overrides it). Give it an aria-label that says what the date is for. To type a date, or to keep the form compact, use DatePicker; for a time of day, TimePicker.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: CalendarDayButton (data-slot calendar-day-button): A day: a size.control.md square button in a gridcell; data-selected, data-today, data-outside, data-disabled and data-range-start, -middle, -end show its state. Calendar renders it; pass it as components.DayButton when wrapping it.
- Props: mode ("single" | "multiple" | "range"); selected (Date | Date[] | DateRange); onSelect ((selected, triggerDate, modifiers, event) => void); required (boolean, default false); disabled (Matcher | Matcher[]); defaultMonth (Date); startMonth (Date); numberOfMonths (number, default 1); showOutsideDays (boolean, default true); showWeekNumber (boolean, default false); locale (Locale (date-fns)); weekStartsOn (0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6); footer (ReactNode); aria-label (string); className (string)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), hover (hover), selected (data-selected), range-middle (data-range-middle), range-start (data-range-start), today (data-today), outside (data-outside), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.compound, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-bg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xl, space.stack.sm, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: Each month is a role="grid" named by its month; the days are buttons in gridcells whose labels give the full date and say when it is today or selected (aria-selected on the cell). One day is in the tab order (the chosen day, else today, else the first day); the arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End to the week's start and end, PageUp and PageDown a month (with Shift a year), and Enter or Space chooses. The caption is a polite live region, so moving to another month announces it; the navigation buttons are named "Go to the Previous Month" and "Go to the Next Month" (the labels prop renames them) and are aria-disabled at the limits. Disabled days are skipped as choices and struck through as well as dimmed; today carries a border and the strong weight besides its colour. Give the calendar an aria-label that says what the date is for; pass a date-fns locale to have the labels in the user's language.

### Card

[card.json](card.json): Fluent 2's Card: a bounded surface that groups one subject, a translucent layer over the backdrop with a hairline and radius 8, with a header (title, description, action), content and a footer; padding follows density.

Usage: Use Card for one subject among several on a page: a connection on the start screen, a saved query, a metric with its Stat. Compose Card > CardHeader (CardTitle, CardDescription, CardAction), CardContent, CardFooter; every part is optional. appearance="filled" (default) is a layer over the backdrop, "filled-alternative" a lighter layer for a card inside another, "outline" a hairline only, "subtle" no edge. Do not nest cards, and do not use one as a page section with a single child: a heading and Separator are lighter. For a list of many records use Table. The old variant prop (outline, raised = filled, inset = filled-alternative) still works for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: CardHeader (data-slot card-header): The top of the card: title and action on the first line, description below.; CardTitle (data-slot card-title): The heading, an <h3> by default; render another level with render.; CardDescription (data-slot card-description): One or two lines under the title.; CardAction (data-slot card-action): Buttons or a menu trigger at the header's end.; CardContent (data-slot card-content): The body.; CardFooter (data-slot card-footer): Actions or facts at the bottom, in a row that wraps.
- appearance: filled, filled-alternative, outline, subtle
- Props: appearance ("filled" | "filled-alternative" | "outline" | "subtle", default "filled"); variant ("outline" | "raised" | "inset", deprecated: use appearance); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.bg.layer, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, elevation.layer.shadow, font.sans, radius.lg, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.stack.md, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight
- Accessibility: A plain grouping element; render an <article> or <section> when the card is a self-contained item or a labelled region. CardTitle is a heading (<h3>), so screen-reader users can jump between cards; pick the level that fits the page with render. Not focusable itself; the controls inside are reached in reading order. Long titles and descriptions wrap (wrap-break-word), so nothing is cut off at any width or density.

### Chart

[chart.json](chart.json): Bar, line and area charts drawn as SVG from data in the colour-blind-safe chart.cat roles, with axes, legend, keyboard-readable tooltip, a hidden data table, decimation for long series, and an inline sparkline.

Usage: Use Chart for a small set of series over categories or time: statements per hour (bar), connections by state (stacked area), latency over the last N statements (line). Pass data (one object per category), x (the category field) and series ({ key, label, color? }); aria-label says what the chart shows. stacked stacks bars or areas; valueFormat and xFormat format numbers and categories. Long series are decimated to the plot width. ChartSparkline is a tiny trend line for a table cell or a Stat. For one number use Stat; for exact values use Table. Charts are built here on SVG (Base UI has none; the project adds no chart library).

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: ChartLegend (data-slot chart-legend): The legend list: each series' swatch (colour and dash) and name.; ChartTooltip (data-slot chart-tooltip): The box with the category and each series' value.; ChartSparkline (data-slot chart-sparkline): A tiny inline line, role="img" with a summary label; values, color, area.
- Props: type ("bar" | "line" | "area", default "bar"); data (Record<string, unknown>[]); x (string, default "\"x\""); series ({ key: string; label: string; color?: 1..8 }[]); stacked (boolean, default false); valueFormat ((value: number) => string); xFormat ((value: unknown) => string); legend (boolean); grid (boolean, default true); activeIndex (number | null); defaultActiveIndex (number | null); onActiveIndexChange ((index: number | null) => void); aria-label (string); emptyText (ReactNode, default "\"No data\""); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: chart.cat.1, chart.cat.2, chart.cat.3, chart.cat.4, chart.cat.5, chart.cat.6, chart.cat.7, chart.cat.8, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.surface, color.border.default, color.border.muted, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.ring, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, radius.lg, radius.sm, ring.offset, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.xs, size.icon.md, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, size.track, space.inline.lg, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, z.tooltip
- Accessibility: The plot is one tab stop (role="group", aria-roledescription="chart", named by aria-label); Left and Right move between categories, Home and End to the ends, Escape clears; a polite live region reads the category and each series' value. A visually hidden table (caption, column and row headers) holds the data and describes the plot (aria-describedby); above 1,000 rows a summary of each series' range replaces it. The SVG itself is aria-hidden. chart.cat colours are colour-blind safe, and series differ by more than colour: lines and areas have their own dash pattern and marker shape (shown in the legend), bars keep their order. ChartSparkline is role="img" with a label that states first, last, lowest and highest values. Nothing animates.

### Checkbox

[checkbox.json](checkbox.json): A checkbox on Base UI's Checkbox, ticked, unticked or mixed, in three sizes, with CheckboxGroup for several checkboxes sharing one value and a parent "select all".

Usage: Use Checkbox for a yes/no choice that is applied when the form is submitted ("Include column headers"), and CheckboxGroup for picking any number of options from a short list. Wrap each checkbox and its text in a FieldLabel inside a Field; in a group, put a FieldLegend first and each option in a FieldItem. With TanStack Form wire checked, onCheckedChange and onBlur (or the group's value and onValueChange) to the field. For a setting that takes effect at once use Switch; for one choice out of several, RadioGroup; for a long list, a MultiSelect. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/checkbox
- Parts: CheckboxGroup (data-slot checkbox-group): Checkboxes sharing one string[] value, a column with gap space.stack.sm; a fieldset named by its FieldLegend.
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: checked (boolean); defaultChecked (boolean, default false); onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean, details) => void); indeterminate (boolean, default false); value (string); parent (boolean, default false); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLSpanElement>)
- States: hover (hover), checked (data-checked), indeterminate (data-indeterminate), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-active, color.accent.compound-fg, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.xs, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, size.icon.xs, space.stack.sm
- Accessibility: Renders a <span role="checkbox"> with aria-checked (true, false or mixed) and a hidden native input for forms; Tab reaches it and Space toggles it. Label it by wrapping it in a FieldLabel with its text; the text then toggles it too and enlarges the target beyond the 14 to 20 px box (WCAG 2.2 target size). A group is a fieldset named by its FieldLegend; a FieldDescription inside a FieldItem describes that option only. Ticked and mixed are shown by a check or a dash as well as the accent fill; the unticked border is color.border.strong (3:1 on every surface). Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

### Code

[code.json](code.json): Inline code in running text (a SQLSTATE, an identifier, a digest) as a <code> in text.code-sm; long values break anywhere.

Usage: Use Code inside a sentence for something the user might type or copy: a SQLSTATE, a table name, a digest or a fingerprint. variant="plain" drops the background inside dense places. For several lines use CodeBlock; for keyboard keys use Kbd; for an editable value use CodeInput.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: default, plain
- Props: variant ("default" | "plain", default "default"); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, font.mono, radius.sm, space.inline.xs, text.code-sm.leading, text.code-sm.size, text.code-sm.tracking, text.code-sm.weight
- Accessibility: A <code> element read in place with the sentence; render <samp> for program output, which is semantically different. color.fg.default on color.bg.inset is contrast-checked as text. Long unbroken values break anywhere (break-all) so they never force horizontal scrolling. Not focusable; to make it copyable, put a copy IconButton next to it.

### CodeBlock

[code-block.json](code-block.json): Read-only, highlighted code in editor.* and syntax.* colours, with line numbers, highlighted lines, a title bar and copy; virtualized above 1,000 lines.

Usage: Use CodeBlock to show code the user reads or copies but does not edit: a statement in the history, a table's DDL, a plugin manifest, diagnostics. language highlights sql (PostgreSQL) or json with the same grammars and colours as CodeInput and SqlEditor; highlightLines marks an error's line; title adds a bar (copy sits there). Give it a height or max-h-* class to scroll. Above virtualizeAfter (1,000) lines only the lines in view are rendered and lines stay on one line. For a single token in a sentence use Code; to edit, SqlEditor or CodeInput; for a JSON value to explore, JsonViewer.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- appearance: editor, inset
- Props: code (string); appearance ("editor" | "inset", default "editor"); language ("text" | "sql" | "json", default "text"); lineNumbers (boolean); startLine (number, default 1); highlightLines (number[]); wrap (boolean, default false); title (ReactNode); copyable (boolean, default "true in the editor appearance"); onCopy ((code: string) => void); virtualizeAfter (number, default 1000); marks ({ starts: readonly number[]; length: number }); currentMark (number); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: highlighted (data-highlighted), wrap (data-wrap), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.inset, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, editor.bg, editor.fg, editor.gutter, editor.line-highlight, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.icon.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, syntax.comment, syntax.constant, syntax.identifier, syntax.keyword, syntax.number, syntax.operator, syntax.string, syntax.type, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: The code is in <pre><code> inside a focusable role="region" named by aria-label or the title, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys. Line numbers are aria-hidden, so screen readers read the code, not the numbers. The copy button is an IconButton ("Copy code", then "Copied"), and a polite status announces "Copied to the clipboard". Virtualized blocks keep only the lines in view in the DOM; screen readers read those, and Copy gives the whole text. Colours are the editor.* and syntax.* roles, which the token build checks for contrast on editor.bg.

### CodeEditor

[code-editor.json](code-editor.json): A code editor on Monaco for JSON, YAML, Protobuf, jq, plain text and languages an app registers, loaded lazily from the app's own bundle (no CDN, no network), themed from the editor.* and syntax.* tokens of its region, with JSON Schema validation, the app's completion, markers by line and column, Mod+Enter to submit, a diff view, and a one-line mode in Fluent's input frame.

Usage: Use CodeEditor for structured text the user writes or reviews: a message payload in the Composer (language="json" with the schema's JSON Schema: validation, completion and hovers, onDiagnosticsChange for a status line), a manifest to apply (language="yaml" with diff={{ original }} to review a change), a .proto file. For a query, a filter or a JSON value on one line, set singleLine (Enter submits, line breaks become spaces) with size as Input's, and give completion for the app's own suggestions (search attributes, saved queries, fields; Ctrl+Space opens them). A language of the app's own goes through registerCodeLanguage(id, setup) in @/lib/monaco, then language="<id>". Mod+Enter calls onSubmit with the text. markers take 1-based lines and columns (a codec's, parser's or server's error position). Monaco loads on first mount; until then a textarea with the same text and keys stands in. Schemas are given, never fetched. Use SqlEditor for SQL, JsonViewer or CodeBlock to show code.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- variant: outline, ghost
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: variant ("outline" | "ghost", default "outline"); language ("json" | "yaml" | "protobuf" | "plaintext" | "jq" | string, default "json"); singleLine (boolean, default false); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); invalid (boolean, default false); completion (CodeCompletion); value (string); defaultValue (string, default ""); onValueChange ((value: string) => void); onSubmit ((value: string) => void); jsonSchema (object); markers (CodeMarker[]); onDiagnosticsChange ((diagnostics: CodeDiagnostic[]) => void); diff ({ original: string }); readOnly (boolean, default false); placeholder (string); lineNumbers (boolean, default true); rows (number); maxRows (number); tabMovesFocus (boolean, default false); aria-label (string); onEditorReady ((editor, monaco) => void); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focused (data-focused), focus-visible (data-focus-visible), loading (data-loading), read-only (data-readonly), invalid (data-invalid), single-line (data-single-line)
- Tokens: color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.subtle, color.fg.subtle, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, editor.bg, editor.cursor, editor.fg, editor.gutter, editor.selection, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.md, size.panel.xs, space.control.x, space.inset.sm, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.code-sm.leading, text.code-sm.size, text.code-sm.tracking, text.code-sm.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: Monaco's text area has the accessible name (aria-label, or aria-labelledby on a visible label); the fallback textarea carries the same name until Monaco has loaded. Tab indents; Ctrl+M toggles Tab moving focus (tabMovesFocus starts in that mode) so keyboard users can leave the editor. Problems are underlined and announced on hover and with F8; onDiagnosticsChange lets the app also show them as text. Focus shows the double ring on the frame: ring.width in color.ring around ring.inner-width in color.ring-inner. singleLine: Enter submits like a form field and Tab leaves the editor; Ctrl+Space opens the suggestions, which Monaco announces as a list; set aria-label or aria-labelledby as for an Input.

### CodeInput

[code-input.json](code-input.json): A small code field on CodeMirror 6: one line (Enter submits) or several, PostgreSQL or JSON highlighting in the syntax.* colours, a read-only pretty viewer for JSON; themed through the token CSS variables and usable inside a Field.

Usage: Use CodeInput for code that fits in a form: one-line SQL conditions and filters (Enter calls onSubmit), short JSON or SQL values (multiline, rows), and showing a cell or JSON value read-only (pretty pretty-prints JSON). Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel, like Input; the value is also in a hidden form control (name, required). Use SqlEditor for whole queries and Textarea for prose.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/input
- size: sm, md, lg
- Props: size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); value (string); defaultValue (string, default ""); onValueChange ((value: string) => void); language ("text" | "sql" | "json", default "text"); multiline (boolean, default false); rows (number, default 3); pretty (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); placeholder (string); onSubmit ((value: string) => void); name (string); required (boolean); aria-label (string); aria-invalid (boolean | "true" | "false"); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focused (data-focused), multiline (data-multiline), read-only (data-readonly), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.subtle, color.status.danger.border, editor.fg, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, opacity.disabled, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.lg, space.inset.sm
- Accessibility: The text area is CodeMirror's contenteditable with role textbox and aria-multiline; inside a Field it takes the FieldLabel (aria-labelledby), the description and error (aria-describedby) and aria-invalid from the Field; on its own, give it aria-label. Tab and Shift+Tab always leave the field (no indentation with Tab), so focus is never trapped; a FieldLabel click focuses the text area. Enter submits a one-line field (onSubmit), as in a text input; in a multi-line one it inserts a line break. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo. Read-only and pretty fields stay focusable so the text can be read, selected and copied by keyboard (aria-readonly); disabled ones leave the tab order (aria-disabled). Syntax colours are syntax.* roles, contrast-checked on the editor background in every mode; colour is never the only signal of an error (FieldError text, the danger border). Focus shows a ring of ring.width in color.ring on the frame.

### Collapsible

[collapsible.json](collapsible.json): One section that shows and hides its panel: a quiet text trigger with a turning chevron and a panel that fades in.

- Accessibility: The trigger is a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the panel; Enter and Space toggle it. The panel is removed from the DOM (or hidden with keepMounted) while closed, so its content is not read or reached by Tab. ### Combobox

[combobox.json](combobox.json): One choice from a long list, typed to filter, on Base UI's Combobox: an input in an Input-like frame with clear and open buttons, and a popup of filtered items, groups, a no-results line and a status line, in three sizes.

Usage: Use Combobox when the user picks one value from a list too long to scan (tables, roles, time zones) or knows what to type.
