### Popover

[popover.json](popover.json): A small non-modal panel attached to a control, on Base UI's Popover: a trigger, and a popup on elevation.flyout (color.bg.overlay) with an optional title, description, controls and a close action, placed on any side of the trigger.

Usage: Use Popover for a few controls or a short explanation that belongs to one control and should not block the page: run options under an icon button, the details of a status badge, a colour picker. Compose it as Popover > PopoverTrigger (render a Button or an IconButton) + PopoverContent (side, align) > PopoverTitle, PopoverDescription, Fields, PopoverClose rendering a Button. It is not modal: the user can click elsewhere and it closes. For text that only names or explains a control on hover, use Tooltip; for a preview of a link on hover, HoverCard; for a list of actions, DropdownMenu; for a task that must be finished or cancelled, Dialog.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/popover
- Parts: PopoverTrigger (data-slot popover-trigger): Opens and closes the popover; unstyled, render a Button or IconButton through render. aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded.; PopoverContent (data-slot popover-content): The portal, the positioner and the popup.; PopoverTitle (data-slot popover-title): An <h2> in type.body-strong that names the popup.; PopoverDescription (data-slot popover-description): A <p> in color.fg.muted that describes the popup.; PopoverClose (data-slot popover-close): Closes the popover; unstyled, render a Button through render.
- Props: open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); modal (boolean | "trap-focus", default false); openOnHover (boolean, default false); side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "inline-start" | "inline-end", default "bottom"); align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "center"); sideOffset (number); initialFocus (RefObject<HTMLElement> | boolean); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.panel.sm, space.inline.sm, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The trigger has aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; the popup is role="dialog", named by PopoverTitle and described by PopoverDescription when they are there. Enter or Space on the trigger opens it and moves focus into the popup; Tab moves through its controls and out of it, which closes it; Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger. A press outside closes it; it is not modal, so the page stays usable and is not hidden from assistive technology. An icon trigger is an IconButton with an aria-label. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the slide and fade transitions off. The popup takes the trigger's theme and density even in a scoped region, and sits at z.popover, so a popover opened from a dialog is above it.

### Progress

[progress.json](progress.json): A bar that shows how far a task has got, with an optional label and formatted value; value={null} is indeterminate.

Usage: Use Progress for a task with measurable progress: an export, a large fetch, a memory budget. Pass value and max, or value={null} while the total is unknown. label names the task (and the bar); showValue prints the formatted value (format, getAriaValueText for "412,000 of 1,000,000 rows"). variant shows the outcome: success, warning, danger. For a short unknown wait use Spinner; for loading content with a known shape use Skeleton.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/progress
- Parts: ProgressLabel (data-slot progress-label): The task's name; Progress renders it from label.; ProgressValue (data-slot progress-value): The formatted value; Progress renders it with showValue.
- variant: accent, success, warning, danger
- size: sm, md
- Props: value (number | null); max (number, default 100); min (number, default 0); label (ReactNode); showValue (boolean, default false); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); getAriaValueText ((formatted: string, value: number | null) => string); variant ("accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", default "accent"); size ("sm" | "md", default "sm"); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: indeterminate (data-indeterminate)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.bg.inset, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.success.solid, color.status.warning.solid, font.sans, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, size.track, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and a formatted aria-valuetext (getAriaValueText for units such as rows); no aria-valuenow while indeterminate. label is the bar's accessible name (aria-labelledby); without one, pass aria-label. The outcome is in the label text ("Export failed at row 180,224"), not only the indicator colour. The width change and the indeterminate slide stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

### RadioGroup

[radio-group.json](radio-group.json): One choice out of several, on Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio: a fieldset of radios named by a FieldLegend, each option in a FieldItem with its own label and description, in three sizes.

Usage: Use RadioGroup when the user must pick exactly one of two to about six options and should see them all at once (TLS mode, line endings). Put it in a Field, a FieldLegend first, then a FieldItem per option with a FieldLabel around a RadioGroupItem and its text, and a FieldDescription when the option needs explaining. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur to the field; an empty value means nothing is chosen yet. For more options use Select; for a choice that applies at once in a toolbar, ToggleGroup; for yes/no, Checkbox or Switch. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/radio-group
- Parts: RadioGroupItem (data-slot radio-group-item): One radio, a circle with color.border.strong with a color.accent.compound stroke and a dot in color.accent.compound when chosen.
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string); defaultValue (string); onValueChange ((value: string, details) => void); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), checked (data-checked), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, size.icon.xs, space.stack.sm
- Accessibility: Renders a <div role="radiogroup"> named by its FieldLegend (aria-labelledby), with a <span role="radio"> and aria-checked per option, and hidden native inputs for forms. Tab enters the group at the chosen radio (or the first) and leaves it; arrow keys move the choice, skipping disabled radios. Wrap each radio and its text in a FieldLabel: the text chooses it too, which enlarges the target beyond the 14 to 20 px circle (WCAG 2.2 target size). A FieldDescription inside the FieldItem describes that option only. The chosen radio shows a dot as well as the accent stroke (color.accent.compound is 3:1 on every surface); the border is color.border.strong (3:1). Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

### RelativeTime

[relative-time.json](relative-time.json): A time relative to now ("in 14 min", "2 s ago") in a <time datetime>, kept current, with the absolute time in a Tooltip and as hidden text.

Usage: Use RelativeTime where how long ago or how soon matters more than the clock time: a grant's expiry, "last run" in the status line, when a connection was created. date takes a Date, an ISO string or epoch ms; timeZone sets the absolute time's zone ("UTC"). It updates itself; pass now to freeze it. tooltip={false} drops the Tooltip (and the tab stop) in long lists. For a timestamp in a data cell, show the absolute value instead.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Props: date (Date | string | number); now (number); live (boolean, default true); locale (string); style ("long" | "short" | "narrow", default "short"); timeZone (string); tooltip (boolean, default true); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLTimeElement>)
- States: tooltip (data-tooltip), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.fg.subtle, color.ring, color.ring-inner, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width
- Accessibility: A <time> with a machine-readable datetime; screen readers read the relative text followed by the absolute time from visually hidden text, so nothing depends on the tooltip. With a tooltip the time is in the tab order and the Tooltip opens on focus as well as hover. Not a live region: the text updates silently (an announcing countdown would never stop). Announce an expiry with a Toast or Alert instead. Formatting uses the browser's Intl APIs in the user's locale; nothing is downloaded.

### Resizable

[resizable.json](resizable.json): Panes the user resizes by dragging or with the keyboard: a group of panels with focusable separator handles between them (ARIA window splitter).

Usage: Use Resizable for an app layout whose panes the user sizes: DBee's sidebar beside the editor, the editor above the results. Compose Resizable (orientation) > ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel …; panels and handles are direct children; nest a vertical group inside a panel for a grid of panes. Sizes are percentages: defaultSize, minSize, maxSize per panel, or sizes and onSizesChange on the group to persist them. collapsible lets Enter on the handle collapse the panel before it. Give the group a sized parent (it fills it). For a fixed rule between sections use Separator; for a collapsible app sidebar with an icon rail use Sidebar.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: ResizablePanel (data-slot resizable-panel): One pane: defaultSize, minSize, maxSize, collapsible, collapsedSize (percent).; ResizableHandle (data-slot resizable-handle): The boundary between two panels; withGrip draws a grip, disabled fixes it, aria-label names it.
- Props: orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); sizes (number[]); onSizesChange ((sizes: number[]) => void); keyboardStep (number, default 5); children (ReactNode); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: vertical (data-[orientation=vertical]), hover (hover), dragging (data-dragging), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.bg.inset, color.border.focus, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.mono, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.xs, size.track, space.inset.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight, z.base
- Accessibility: Each handle is a focusable role="separator" (window splitter pattern) with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax giving the size of the panel before it, and aria-controls naming that panel. Arrow keys move the handle by keyboardStep percent (Left/Right in a horizontal group, mirrored in right-to-left; Up/Down in a vertical one); Home and End take the panel to its minimum and maximum; Enter collapses and restores a collapsible panel. Name each handle with aria-label ("Resize sidebar"); aria-orientation is that of the rule (vertical in a horizontal group). Dragging moves focus to the handle, so keyboard and pointer use the same element. The hit area is wider than the rule (size.track on each side).

### ScrollArea

[scroll-area.json](scroll-area.json): A scroll container with thin themed overlay scrollbars that fade in while hovering or scrolling; the viewport scrolls natively.

Usage: Use ScrollArea for a panel, popover body or log that scrolls inside a fixed height (give it h-full in a sized panel or a max-h-panel-* class). scrollbars picks which bars are drawn; the content scrolls on both axes when it overflows. For long lists, put the virtualized component inside and read the viewport through viewportRef. The page itself should keep the browser's scrollbar.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/scroll-area
- Props: children (ReactNode); scrollbars ("vertical" | "horizontal" | "both", default "vertical"); viewportRef (Ref<HTMLDivElement>); onViewportScroll ((event: UIEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void); aria-label (string); aria-labelledby (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), hovering (data-hovering), scrolling (data-scrolling), hover (hover)
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.scrollbar.thumb, color.scrollbar.thumb-hover, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.track
- Accessibility: The viewport scrolls natively, so wheel, touch, and the arrow, Page and Home/End keys work once it has focus. When the content overflows the viewport is in the tab order (tabIndex 0) and shows a focus ring, so keyboard users can scroll it. Pass aria-label or aria-labelledby when the region needs a name; the viewport then has role="region". The overlay scrollbars are pointer aids; they are not focusable and carry no information the keyboard lacks.

### SearchInput

[search-input.json](search-input.json): A search box on InputGroup and Base UI's Input: a search icon, type="search", and a Clear button (and Escape) while there is text, in Fluent's small, medium and large.

Usage: Use SearchInput to filter or search a list as the user types: tables in a schema browser, rows of a result, settings. - Accessibility: The text control is a native <input type="search"> (role searchbox); name it with a FieldLabel or aria-label, not only a placeholder. The Clear button is a native <button> named "Clear search"; it returns focus to the input. Escape clears as well, and is left to the page (a dialog) when the box is empty. Announce how many results match in a role="status" element next to it; the box itself does not. The search icon is decorative (aria-hidden) and clicking it focuses the input. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

### Select

[select.json](select.json): One choice from a list, on Base UI's Select: a trigger that looks like an Input and shows the chosen label, and a listbox popup with items, groups and separators, in three sizes.

Usage: Use Select when the user picks one value from a fixed list of about five to thirty options they need not type (SSL mode, engine, isolation level). Put it in a Field after a FieldLabel, pass items (a record of value to label, or { value, label } objects) so the trigger shows the label before the popup opens, and list the options as SelectItem children, grouped with SelectGroup and SelectGroupLabel when that helps. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onOpenChange (blur on close) to the field; null means nothing is chosen. For two to six options that should all be visible use RadioGroup; for long or searchable lists, Combobox; for several values, MultiSelect. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/select
- Parts: SelectItem (data-slot select-item): One option, role="option": its text, and a check mark while chosen; color.interactive.hover while highlighted.; SelectGroup (data-slot select-group): A group of options, role="group", named by its SelectGroupLabel.; SelectGroupLabel (data-slot select-group-label): A group's heading in type.caption and color.fg.subtle.; SelectSeparator (data-slot select-separator): A 1 px line in color.border.default between options or groups.
- appearance: outline, underline, filled-darker, filled-lighter
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: items (Record<string, ReactNode> | { value, label }[]); value (Value | null); defaultValue (Value | null); onValueChange ((value: Value | null, details) => void); placeholder (ReactNode); appearance ("outline" | "underline" | "filled-darker" | "filled-lighter", default "outline"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); open (boolean); name (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); aria-label (string); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), open (data-popup-open), entering (data-starting-style), placeholder (data-placeholder), highlighted (data-highlighted), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer-alt, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.surface, color.border.control-bottom, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.hover, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.stroke, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, shadow.focus-underline, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body-2.leading, text.body-2.size, text.body-2.tracking, text.body-2.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The trigger is a <button role="combobox"> with aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded, named by its FieldLabel (aria-labelledby) or aria-label; the popup is a role="listbox" of role="option" items with aria-selected. Enter, Space, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the popup; arrow keys, Home and End move the highlight, typing jumps to the option that starts with the text, Enter chooses and Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger. Disabled options are skipped by the keyboard and shown in color.fg.disabled; a group's label names the group (aria-labelledby). The chosen option shows a check mark as well as its place in the trigger, so the state does not rest on colour; the trigger's bottom edge is color.border.control-bottom (3:1 on every fill and surface). The popup takes the trigger's theme and density even when they are set on a region rather than <html>, so its contrast matches the page it opened from.

### Separator

[separator.json](separator.json): A thin rule between groups of content, horizontal or vertical, in a border role at border.width.1.

Usage: Use Separator between sections of a panel, between groups of controls in a Toolbar or StatusBar (orientation="vertical"), or between the facts of a summary line. It is announced as a separator; for pure decoration use a border on the container instead. Between resizable panes use Resizable's handle, not a Separator.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/separator
- variant: default, muted, strong
- Props: variant ("default" | "muted" | "strong", default "default"); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: horizontal (data-[orientation=horizontal]), vertical (data-[orientation=vertical])
- Tokens: border.width.1, color.border.muted, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle
- Accessibility: Renders a <div role="separator"> with aria-orientation; screen readers announce the boundary between groups. Not focusable and not interactive (a movable pane divider is Resizable's handle). Thickness is border.width.1 and colour a border role, so it never carries information on its own.

### Sheet

[sheet.json](sheet.json): A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the window over a scrim, on Base UI's Dialog: right, left, top or bottom, three widths, a header, a scrolling body, a pinned footer and a close button.

Usage: Use Sheet for a form or a detail view that belongs beside the page rather than in front of it: edit a connection, a cell's full value, filters. Compose it as Sheet > SheetTrigger (render a Button; or open it through open) + SheetContent > SheetHeader (SheetTitle, SheetDescription), SheetBody (the Fields; it scrolls), SheetFooter (SheetClose rendering a Button, then the primary action). side picks the edge (right by default) and size the width of a left or right sheet; a top or bottom sheet spans the window and is as tall as its content. Every sheet needs a SheetTitle. For a short task in the middle of the screen use Dialog; for a decision use AlertDialog; for a sidebar that stays open next to the content use Sidebar.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/dialog
- Parts: SheetTrigger (data-slot sheet-trigger): Opens the sheet; unstyled, render a Button through render.; SheetContent (data-slot sheet-content): The portal with the scrim and the sheet, plus a close IconButton unless showClose is false.; SheetBackdrop (data-slot sheet-backdrop): The scrim; SheetContent renders it.; SheetHeader (data-slot sheet-header): The title and description, stacked, leaving room for the close button.; SheetTitle (data-slot sheet-title): An <h2> in text.subtitle-1 (Fluent's dialog title) that names the sheet.; SheetDescription (data-slot sheet-description): A <p> in color.fg.muted that describes the sheet.; SheetBody (data-slot sheet-body): The content; takes the free height and scrolls.; SheetFooter (data-slot sheet-footer): The actions, pinned at the bottom of the sheet.; SheetClose (data-slot sheet-close): Closes the sheet; unstyled, render a Button through render.
- side: right, left, top, bottom
- size: sm, md, lg
- Props: side ("right" | "left" | "top" | "bottom", default "right"); size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean, details) => void); disablePointerDismissal (boolean, default false); showClose (boolean, default true); closeLabel (string, default "Close"); className (string)
- States: open (data-starting-style), closing (data-ending-style)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.bg.scrim, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.disabled, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.dialog.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.gentle, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.icon.lg, size.panel.lg, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inset.lg, space.inset.md, space.stack.md, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, text.subtitle-1.leading, text.subtitle-1.size, text.subtitle-1.tracking, text.subtitle-1.weight, z.modal, z.overlay
- Accessibility: The sheet is role="dialog", named by SheetTitle and described by SheetDescription; while it is open the page behind is inert and hidden from assistive technology. Opening moves focus into the sheet; Tab stays inside; Escape or a press on the scrim closes it and focus returns to the trigger. The close button is an IconButton with an accessible name and a visible focus ring. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the slide off (motion-reduce:transition-none); the sheet appears in place. The sheet takes the theme and density of the region it is declared in.

### Sidebar

[sidebar.json](sidebar.json): The side panel of an app shell: a provider with the open state and a Ctrl/Cmd+B toggle, a size.panel.xs panel on either side that collapses to an icon rail (labels become tooltips) or hides, a header, a scrolling content area, a footer, labelled groups, menus of buttons or links, a toggle and the main area beside it.

Usage: Use Sidebar for the persistent side panel of an application: DBee's connections and schema tree, a settings navigation. Compose it as SidebarProvider (open, onOpenChange; hotkey "b" for Ctrl/Cmd+B) > Sidebar (side, collapsible: "icon" or "offcanvas") with SidebarHeader, SidebarContent (SidebarGroup > SidebarGroupLabel + SidebarMenu > SidebarMenuItem > SidebarMenuButton with icon, active, tooltip; or a Tree), SidebarFooter; then SidebarInset for the main area with a SidebarTrigger. Name the Sidebar with aria-label. For a temporary panel over the page use Sheet; for top navigation, NavigationMenu; resizing the panel is wave 3's Resizable.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: SidebarProvider (data-slot sidebar-provider): The shell row holding the open state and the hotkey.; SidebarHeader (data-slot sidebar-header): The top of the panel.; SidebarContent (data-slot sidebar-content): The scrolling middle of the panel.; SidebarFooter (data-slot sidebar-footer): The bottom of the panel.; SidebarGroup (data-slot sidebar-group): A section, role="group" named by its label.; SidebarGroupLabel (data-slot sidebar-group-label): A section heading in type.caption and color.fg.subtle; visually hidden in the icon rail.; SidebarMenu (data-slot sidebar-menu): A list of entries, a <ul>.; SidebarMenuItem (data-slot sidebar-menu-item): One entry, an <li>.; SidebarMenuButton (data-slot sidebar-menu-button): An entry's button or link (size.control.md): icon and label, aria-current when active; in the icon rail a square with a Tooltip.; SidebarTrigger (data-slot sidebar-trigger): An IconButton that toggles the sidebar, with aria-expanded and aria-controls.; SidebarInset (data-slot sidebar-inset): The main area beside the sidebar, a <main>.
- side: left, right
- Props: open (boolean); onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void); hotkey (string | false, default "b"); side ("left" | "right", default "left"); collapsible ("icon" | "offcanvas" | "none", default "offcanvas"); aria-label (string, default "Sidebar"); icon (ReactNode); active (boolean, default false); tooltip (ReactNode); render (ReactElement); className (string)
- States: collapsed (data-[collapsed=icon]), offcanvas (data-[collapsed=offcanvas]), active (data-active), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.panel.sm, size.panel.xs, space.inline.sm, space.inset.sm, space.inset.xs, space.stack.sm, space.stack.xs, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.caption-1-strong.leading, text.caption-1-strong.size, text.caption-1-strong.tracking, text.caption-1-strong.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight
- Accessibility: The panel is an <aside> landmark named by aria-label; the main area is a <main>; sections are role="group" named by their labels; entries are buttons or links in a list, the current one with aria-current="page". SidebarTrigger is an IconButton named "Toggle sidebar" with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the panel; Ctrl+B (Cmd+B on macOS) toggles it too (aria-keyshortcuts). In the icon rail the labels stay in the accessibility tree (visually hidden) and show as tooltips on hover and focus, so entries keep their names. An off-canvas sidebar that is closed is display:none, so its content leaves the tab order. The width change transitions over motion.duration.base; prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns it off.

### Skeleton

[skeleton.json](skeleton.json): An aria-hidden placeholder in the shape of loading content (a text line, a block, a circle) that pulses slowly.

Usage: Use Skeleton while content with a known shape loads: tree rows, a card, a line of text. Size blocks and circles with classes (h-control-sm w-panel-xs, size-control-md); text lines take the body text size. Mark the loading region aria-busy and name it (aria-label "Loading tables") or add a labelled Spinner. Keep the skeleton's layout close to the real content so nothing jumps. For an unknown shape use Spinner; for measurable progress use Progress.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: text, block, circle
- Props: variant ("text" | "block" | "circle", default "block"); animated (boolean, default true); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.bg.inset, radius.md, radius.sm, text.body.size
- Accessibility: Every skeleton is aria-hidden; the loading region carries aria-busy and a name (or a labelled Spinner), so screen readers announce loading once. Remove aria-busy when the content arrives so the region is read again. The pulse runs through the Web Animations API at eight motion.duration.slow per beat and never under prefers-reduced-motion. Not focusable.

### Slider

[slider.json](slider.json): A slider on Base UI's Slider: one value or a range with two thumbs, horizontal or vertical, on a size.track track with an accent indicator, in three thumb sizes.

Usage: Use Slider for a value in a known range where the position matters more than the exact number (a sample percentage, a zoom level), or for a range with two thumbs. Put it in a Field with a FieldLabel, and show the current value in the label or next to it; name each thumb of a range with getAriaLabel. With TanStack Form wire value, onValueChange and onBlur (onValueCommitted for work that should run only when the user lets go). For an exact number, use NumberInput, or pair the two. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/slider
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (number | number[]); defaultValue (number | number[]); onValueChange ((value: number | number[], details) => void); onValueCommitted ((value: number | number[], details) => void); min (number, default 0); max (number, default 100); step (number, default 1); largeStep (number, default 10); minStepsBetweenValues (number, default 0); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); aria-label (string); getAriaLabel ((index: number) => string); format (Intl.NumberFormatOptions); name (string); disabled (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), dragging (data-dragging), focus-visible (has-focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-active, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.surface, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.stroke, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, shadow.raised, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, size.track
- Accessibility: Each thumb holds a native <input type="range">, so screen readers announce it as a slider with its value, and Tab reaches each thumb. Arrow keys move by step, PageUp/PageDown and Shift+arrow by largeStep, Home and End to min and max. A FieldLabel names a single thumb; name both thumbs of a range with getAriaLabel ("Minimum length", "Maximum length"). Use format so units are announced. The thumb is an accent disc in a ring of the surface colour (color.accent.compound is 3:1 on every surface); the rail is color.border.strong (3:1) and the selected part color.accent.compound. Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) around the thumb (3:1 on every surface).

### Spinner

[spinner.json](spinner.json): An indeterminate activity indicator: a ring with a turning arc in size.icon.*, a polite status region that names what is loading.

Usage: Use Spinner when something is loading and the wait is short or unknown: a tree node's children, a running query in its tab, a connection opening. Give it a label that says what loads; inside a control that already says so (a Button with loading), pass label={null}. For a wait with known progress use Progress; for content whose shape is known use Skeleton.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- variant: current, accent, muted
- size: sm, md, lg
- Props: label (ReactNode | null, default "\"Loading\""); variant ("current" | "accent" | "muted", default "current"); size ("sm" | "md" | "lg", default "md"); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: 
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.border.default, color.fg.muted, opacity.overlay, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, space.inline.xs
- Accessibility: A labelled spinner is role="status" with visually hidden text, so screen readers announce what is loading; the SVG is aria-hidden. label={null} sets aria-hidden for a spinner inside a control that already reports busy (aria-busy on a loading Button). It turns through the Web Animations API, once per three motion.duration.slow, and never under prefers-reduced-motion; the still arc keeps its meaning. Not focusable.

### SplitButton

[split-button.json](split-button.json): Fluent 2's SplitButton: a main action joined to a menu of its variants, a Button and a chevron IconButton that opens a DropdownMenu (Base UI's Menu), in Button's primary, secondary, outline, subtle and transparent appearances and small, medium and large.

Usage: Use SplitButton when one action is the usual choice and a few close variants should stay one click away: Run (statement under cursor) with Run selection and Explain in the menu, Export CSV with other formats. Put the action's label in children and its handler in onClick, and the menu's DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuLabel and DropdownMenuSeparator in menu; name the menu button with menuLabel. loading shows the action running while the menu stays usable. When there is no usual choice, use a DropdownMenu behind a plain Button; for unrelated actions, separate Buttons. The old variant prop (ghost is subtle) and sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- appearance: primary, secondary, outline, subtle, transparent
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: children (ReactNode); onClick (MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>); menu (ReactNode); menuLabel (string, default "More options"); appearance ("primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "subtle" | "transparent", default "primary"); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); variant ("primary" | "secondary" | "ghost", deprecated: use appearance (ghost is subtle)); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); disabled (boolean, default false); loading (boolean, default false); align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "end"); open (boolean); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLButtonElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), open (data-popup-open), loading (data-loading), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-active, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.bg.disabled, color.bg.layer, color.bg.overlay, color.border.control-bottom-subtle, color.border.default, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.flyout.shadow, font.sans, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.duration.normal, motion.easing.accelerate-mid, motion.easing.decelerate-mid, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.lg, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.icon.lg, size.icon.md, size.icon.xl, size.panel.xs, space.control.x, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.md, space.inset.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.subtitle-2.leading, text.subtitle-2.size, text.subtitle-2.tracking, text.subtitle-2.weight, z.popover
- Accessibility: The control is a role="group" of two buttons, each in the tab order: the action, named by its label, and the menu button, named by menuLabel, with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Enter or Space on the action runs it; on the menu button, Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens the menu with the first item highlighted; Escape closes it and returns focus to the menu button. The menu follows DropdownMenu: arrows, Home, End and typing move, Enter chooses; a press outside closes it. loading keeps the action focusable and sets aria-busy; the divider is a border colour, and the halves are separate buttons, so the split does not rest on colour alone. The menu takes the control's theme and density and sits at z.popover.

### SqlEditor

[sql-editor.json](sql-editor.json): A SQL editor on Monaco, loaded lazily from the app's own bundle (no CDN, no network), themed from the editor.* and syntax.* tokens of its region in every preset, mode and density, with run-at-cursor, error markers and a read-only mode.

Usage: Use SqlEditor for real queries: a query tab (variant="ghost", className="h-full") or a bordered field (variant="outline", the default, 240 px high; set the height with className). Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) calls onRun with the selection, or the statement under the cursor, and the statements it holds; markers take offsets into the text (a PostgreSQL error position minus one). Monaco loads on first mount; until then a textarea with the same text and keys stands in, so nothing waits. Monaco has one theme per page: the editor mounted, focused or rethemed last sets the colours of every editor. Use Textarea for short SQL in a form, CodeInput for one-line expressions, and CodeBlock to show code.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- variant: outline, ghost
- Props: variant ("outline" | "ghost", default "outline"); value (string); defaultValue (string, default ""); onValueChange ((value: string) => void); onRun ((run: SqlRun) => void); markers (SqlMarker[]); readOnly (boolean, default false); language ("pgsql" | "sql", default "pgsql"); placeholder (string); lineNumbers (boolean, default true); tabMovesFocus (boolean, default false); screenReaderOptimized (boolean, default false); aria-label (string, default "SQL editor"); onEditorReady ((editor, monaco) => void); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: focused (data-focused), loading (data-loading), read-only (data-readonly)
- Tokens: color.border.control-bottom, color.border.subtle, color.ring, color.ring-inner, editor.bg, editor.cursor, editor.fg, editor.gutter, editor.selection, font.mono, radius.lg, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.panel.xs, space.inset.sm, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: The text area is Monaco's own input (a textarea or an EditContext with role textbox), named by aria-label ("SQL editor" by default) or aria-labelledby; the stand-in textarea has the same name. Tab indents inside the editor, as code editors do; Ctrl+M (Ctrl+Shift+M on macOS) switches Tab to move focus, and tabMovesFocus starts in that mode, so focus is never trapped. Every action has a key: Ctrl+Enter runs, Ctrl+F finds, Ctrl+/ comments, F8 and Shift+F8 move between error markers, F1 opens Monaco's command list. Error markers are announced through Monaco's hover and the F8 marker widget, not by colour alone; editor.* and syntax.* colours are contrast-checked by the token build in every mode. screenReaderOptimized turns on Monaco's screen reader mode (offer it as a setting); otherwise Monaco detects a screen reader. Focus shows a ring of ring.width in color.ring on the frame. Nothing is fetched: Monaco, its worker and its font come from the app's bundle.

### Stat

[stat.json](stat.json): One number that matters, with its label, an optional change (arrow, words for screen readers, colour by intent) and a description.

Usage: Use Stat for a few key numbers: a query's time and row count, a table's size, connections in use. Compose Stat > StatLabel, StatValue, StatDelta (trend, intent), StatDescription. Format the value in the app (units, grouping). Set intent when up is bad (query time). Put stats in a row or in Cards; for many numbers use Table, for a series use a chart.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: StatLabel (data-slot stat-label): What the number is.; StatValue (data-slot stat-value): The formatted number.; StatDelta (data-slot stat-delta): The change: trend (up, down, flat), intent (positive, negative, neutral), trendLabel.; StatDescription (data-slot stat-description): Context for the number.
- size: sm, md
- Props: size ("sm" | "md", default "md"); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: positive (data-[intent=positive]), negative (data-[intent=negative]), neutral (data-[intent=neutral])
- Tokens: color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.success.fg, font.sans, size.icon.xs, space.inline.xs, space.stack.xs, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.subtitle-1.leading, text.subtitle-1.size, text.subtitle-1.tracking, text.subtitle-1.weight, text.title-2.leading, text.title-2.size, text.title-2.tracking, text.title-2.weight
- Accessibility: Plain text in reading order: label, value, change, description. StatDelta's arrow is aria-hidden and the trend is said in words ("Up 12 %"), so the change never depends on the arrow or the colour. Values use tabular figures so they line up; long labels truncate (put the full label in title if it matters). Not focusable.

### StatusBar

[status-bar.json](status-bar.json): The thin bar at the bottom of an app or pane: one-line status items that truncate, buttons, a spacer, and live items announced politely.

Usage: Use StatusBar at the bottom of the app shell or of a results pane for passive status: connection, row count, elapsed time, cursor position, encoding. Compose StatusBar (aria-label) > StatusBarItem / StatusBarButton, StatusBarSpacer, then the items for the end. Wrap item text in a <span> so it truncates, and put the full text in title. Mark the item that changes after an action (row count) live. For commands use Toolbar; for messages that need attention use Toast or Alert.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: StatusBarItem (data-slot status-bar-item): Status text with an optional icon; live makes it a polite live region.; StatusBarButton (data-slot status-bar-button): An item that does something when pressed.; StatusBarSpacer (data-slot status-bar-spacer): Pushes the following items to the end.
- variant: default, accent
- Props: variant ("default" | "accent", default "default"); aria-label (string); children (ReactNode); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.bg, color.accent.bg-hover, color.accent.fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.subtle, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, font.sans, opacity.disabled, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.xs, size.icon.xs, size.panel.sm, space.inline.xs, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: The bar is a role="group" named by aria-label; plain items are text in reading order and not focusable. A live item is role="status" with aria-live="polite": a row count that changes when a query ends is announced without moving focus. Mark only the items that change after an action. StatusBarButton is a native <button> in the tab order with a focus ring. Truncated text keeps the full value in title; prefer short labels so nothing important is cut.

### Stepper

[stepper.json](stepper.json): The steps of a task done in order: an ordered list of numbered steps joined by lines, showing done (accent, check), current, upcoming and failed steps, horizontal or vertical, with completed steps optionally clickable to go back.

Usage: Use Stepper to show where the user is in a task of three to six ordered steps: add a connection, approve access, connect; a first-run guide. Pass steps ({ title, description?, error? }) and value (the current index; steps.length when all are done); pass onValueChange to let the user return to a completed step; name it with aria-label. It shows progress, it does not hold the steps' content: render the current step's form beside it. For a hierarchy use Breadcrumb; for views the user switches freely, Tabs.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: StepperItem (data-slot stepper-item): One step, an <li> with aria-current="step" when current and data-status; Stepper renders one per step.
- orientation: horizontal, vertical
- Props: steps ({ title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; error?: boolean }[]); value (number); onValueChange ((index: number) => void); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); aria-label (string, default "Progress"); className (string)
- States: complete (data-[status=complete]), current (data-[status=current]), upcoming (data-[status=upcoming]), error (data-[status=error]), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-fg, color.bg.layer, color.border.strong, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.icon.md, space.inline.sm, space.stack.md, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight
- Accessibility: An ordered list named by aria-label; the current step has aria-current="step". Each step's status is visually hidden text after its title (completed, current step, not started, failed), so it does not rest on the circle's colour or icon, which are aria-hidden. With onValueChange, completed steps are buttons in the tab order with a focus ring; upcoming steps are not interactive. Only colours transition; nothing moves.

### Switch

[switch.json](switch.json): An on/off switch on Base UI's Switch: a track that fills with the compound accent and a sliding thumb, in three sizes.

Usage: Use Switch for a setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped ("Auto-commit", "Read-only connection"), in settings panels and side panels. Wrap it in a FieldLabel with its text (the text may come first) inside a Field, and add a FieldDescription for what it does; group related switches in a FieldSet with a FieldLegend. With TanStack Form wire checked, onCheckedChange and onBlur to the field. For a choice that only applies when a form is submitted, use Checkbox; for a toolbar toggle, ToggleButton. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/switch
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: checked (boolean); defaultChecked (boolean, default false); onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean, details) => void); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); size (sm, md, lg) ("sm" | "md" | "lg", deprecated: use small, medium or large); name (string); value (string); uncheckedValue (string); required (boolean, default false); disabled (boolean, default false); readOnly (boolean, default false); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLSpanElement>)
- States: hover (hover), checked (data-checked), focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: color.accent.compound, color.accent.compound-active, color.accent.compound-fg, color.accent.compound-hover, color.bg.disabled, color.border.disabled, color.border.strong, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.border, motion.duration.fast, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.md, size.icon.sm, size.icon.xs
- Accessibility: Renders a <span role="switch"> with aria-checked and a hidden native input for forms; Tab reaches it, Space and Enter flip it. Label it by wrapping it in a FieldLabel with its text; the text flips it too and enlarges the target beyond the track (WCAG 2.2 target size). Name the setting, not the state ("Auto-commit", not "Auto-commit on"). On and off differ by the thumb's position as well as the track colour; off, the track is outlined in color.border.strong and the thumb is color.fg.muted (both at least 3:1). The thumb slides in the reading direction (right in LTR, left in RTL). Focus shows Fluent's accent underline (shadow.focus-underline) (3:1 on every surface).

### Table

[table.json](table.json): Fluent 2's Table on semantic table elements: no shell of its own (it sits on its layer), rows of 44, 34 or 24 px by size under a 32 px header in strong text (the TSK-91 mockup), a subtle divider under each row, hover, press and selection washes, a focus ring inside a focused row; a sticky header that fills only while scrolled, sortable headers, NULL marker, a virtualized body for large row counts, and an opt-in surface appearance (the earlier card).

Usage: Use Table for records with the same columns: a table's columns, indexes, grants, the audit log, a small query result. Compose Table (aria-label, or TableCaption with aria-labelledby) > TableHeader > TableRow > TableHead, then TableBody > TableRow > TableCell, and an optional TableFooter. It is presentational: the app sorts (TableHead sort + onSort), selects (TableRow selected) and pages. Cells keep one line and truncate (wrap lets one wrap); align="end" for numbers; TableNull for SQL NULL. For more than about 1,000 rows, give the Table a height and use TableVirtualBody with count and renderRow; browsers cap an element's height near 33.5 million px, so it serves up to about 760,000 rows at the medium row height (1.4 million at extra-small). Put the Table in a parent that lets it shrink (min-w-0) so wide tables scroll inside it. For streamed Arrow results with cell selection and column resizing use the DataGrid package (TSK-39); for term/value pairs use DescriptionList. The default appearance has no shell: put the Table on a layer, card or dialog; appearance="surface" gives it the earlier card of its own. size="small" or "extra-small" for dense lists.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Parts: TableHeader (data-slot table-header): The <thead>; its heads stick while the body scrolls.; TableBody (data-slot table-body): The <tbody> for rows you render (up to about 1,000).; TableVirtualBody (data-slot table-virtual-body): A <tbody> that renders only the rows in view: count, renderRow, overscan, headerRows.; TableFooter (data-slot table-footer): The <tfoot>.; TableRow (data-slot table-row): A <tr>; selected marks it.; TableHead (data-slot table-head): A column header: align, sort, onSort.; TableCell (data-slot table-cell): A data cell: align, wrap.; TableCaption (data-slot table-caption): What the table lists; names it.; TableNull (data-slot table-null): A SQL NULL, distinct from an empty string.
- variant: plain, striped, bordered
- appearance: transparent, surface
- size: medium, small, extra-small
- Props: variant ("plain" | "striped" | "bordered", default "plain"); appearance ("transparent" | "surface", default "transparent"); size ("medium" | "small" | "extra-small", default "medium"); aria-label (string); aria-labelledby (string); children (ReactNode); className (string); tableClassName (string); ref (Ref<HTMLDivElement>)
- States: hover (hover), selected (data-selected), focus-visible (focus-visible), align-end (data-[align=end]), wrap (data-wrap)
- Tokens: border.width.0, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer, color.bg.surface, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.fg.subtle, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.interactive.selected, color.interactive.selected-hover, color.ring, color.ring-inner, elevation.layer.shadow, font.mono, font.sans, grid.header-bg, grid.null-fg, grid.row-bg-alt, radius.lg, radius.md, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.icon.xs, size.panel.md, size.panel.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.xs, table.cell-padding-x, table.row-height-extra-small, table.row-height-medium, table.row-height-small, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.caption-1.leading, text.caption-1.size, text.caption-1.tracking, text.caption-1.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, z.sticky
- Accessibility: A real <table> with <thead>, <th scope="col"> and <td>, so screen readers announce headers with each cell; name it with aria-label or a TableCaption referenced by aria-labelledby. A labelled table's scroll container is a focusable region, so keyboard users can scroll a tall or wide table with the arrow keys. A sortable column's label is a button; the current order is aria-sort on the <th> and an icon (aria-hidden). TableVirtualBody keeps the semantic table: the <table> has aria-rowcount (all rows plus the header) and each rendered row its aria-rowindex; the spacer rows are aria-hidden. Selected rows set aria-selected; NULL is the word NULL, not a colour; truncated cells should carry the full value in title. Not an interactive grid: no cell focus or arrow-key movement between cells. For that, use the DataGrid (ARIA grid pattern).

### Tabs

[tabs.json](tabs.json): Tabs on Base UI's Tabs with Fluent 2's appearances (transparent underline, subtle wash, Byterygon's enclosed editor tabs) in small, medium and large, horizontal or vertical, with panels; tabs can carry a status icon, be closed with a button or Delete, be reordered by drag or Alt+Shift+Arrow, and carry a count in its own badge, and be grouped behind headings that never overflow.

Usage: Use Tabs to switch between views of the same place: the sections of a Settings dialog (appearance transparent), or DBee's query tabs (appearance enclosed, size small). Compose it as Tabs (value, onValueChange) > TabsList > TabsTrigger per tab (value, icon for a status, children for the title) + TabsContent per tab. For closable tabs pass onClose on each TabsTrigger and keep the tabs in state (Tabs controlled): when the active tab closes, choose the next one. For a number that belongs to a tab (History 1,234, Errors 3) pass count on its TabsTrigger, never in the title: it is drawn in a Badge after the title, neutral unless countTone says it needs attention (danger, warning), hidden at 0 unless showZero, shortened from 10,000 (12.4k) with its full number in a title, and read with the title as one name (countLabel says what it counts: "History, 1,234 events"). For reorderable tabs pass onReorder(value, index) on TabsList and move the tab in your array. For navigation between pages use NavigationMenu or Sidebar; for a choice that filters content in place, ToggleGroup. The old variant prop (line is transparent) and the sm/md sizes still work for one release. For a strip grouped by something (Mightyconsole groups its tabs by tool), put a TabsLabel (value, icon, children) before each open group's tabs and a keepVisible TabsTrigger for each folded group; give the label the words a heading needs ("NATS, 4 tabs").

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/tabs
- Parts: TabsList (data-slot tabs-list): role="tablist" in a strip (data-slot="tabs-strip") that never scrolls: tabs that do not fit go to a "More tabs" menu at its end (Fluent's TabList overflow), the selected one always stays visible; onReorder makes the tabs movable; moreLabel names the menu button.; TabsTrigger (data-slot tabs-trigger): role="tab" with aria-selected and aria-controls: icon, truncated title, and a close button when closable.; TabsLabel (data-slot tabs-label-item): An item of the strip that is not a tab (a group's heading before its tabs, Mightyconsole's tab groups): never selected, passed by the arrow keys, always kept out of More tabs; its value takes part in onReorder, so it is draggable when the tabs are.; TabsContent (data-slot tabs-content): role="tabpanel", labelled by its tab.
- appearance: transparent, subtle, enclosed
- size: small, medium, large
- Props: value (string | number); onValueChange ((value, details) => void); appearance ("transparent" | "subtle" | "enclosed", default "transparent"); variant ("line" | "enclosed", deprecated: use appearance); size ("small" | "medium" | "large", default "medium"); orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical", default "horizontal"); onReorder ((value, index: number) => void); moreLabel (string, default "More tabs"); activateOnFocus (boolean, default false); icon (ReactNode); count (number | null); countLabel (string | [one: string, other: string]); countMore (boolean, default false); countTone ("neutral" | "accent" | "danger" | "warning" | "success" | "info", default "neutral"); showZero (boolean, default false); keepVisible (boolean, default "false"); onClose (() => void); closeLabel (string, default "Close tab"); disabled (boolean, default false); keepMounted (boolean, default false); className (string)
- States: active (data-active), hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled), closable (data-closable), dragging (data-dragging), drop-target (data-[drop=before])
- Tokens: border.width.3, color.accent.compound, color.bg.inset, color.bg.layer, color.bg.layer-alt, color.border.default, color.border.subtle, color.fg.default, color.fg.disabled, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.active, color.interactive.hover, color.neutral.bg, color.neutral.fg, color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.danger.bg, color.status.danger.border, color.status.danger.fg, color.status.danger.solid, color.status.danger.solid-fg, font.mono, font.sans, motion.duration.faster, motion.easing.easy-ease, opacity.disabled, radius.lg, radius.sm, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.md, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.md, size.icon.xs, size.panel.xs, space.control.x, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, space.inset.sm, space.stack.sm, text.body-1-strong.leading, text.body-1-strong.size, text.body-1-strong.tracking, text.body-1-strong.weight, text.body-1.leading, text.body-1.size, text.body-1.tracking, text.body-1.weight, text.body.leading, text.body.size, text.body.tracking, text.body.weight, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight, z.sticky
- Accessibility: The strip is role="tablist" of role="tab" elements with aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel is role="tabpanel" labelled by its tab. Only the active tab is in the tab order. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (ArrowUp and ArrowDown when vertical), Home and End move between tabs; Enter or Space activates the focused tab (or focus activates it with activateOnFocus). A closable tab closes with Delete when focused (aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"); its close button is for the pointer, out of the tab order and hidden from assistive technology so the tablist holds only tabs. Focus moves to the neighbouring tab. A reorderable tab moves with Alt+Shift+ArrowLeft and Alt+Shift+ArrowRight (Up and Down when vertical), announced through aria-keyshortcuts, as well as by drag, so reordering does not need a pointer. A status icon needs a text alternative (role="img" with aria-label, or visually hidden text), since a coloured dot alone carries no meaning. Only colours transition; nothing moves, so reduced motion needs no change. A count is a Badge hidden from assistive technology, and its number is read as part of the tab's one name through visually hidden text ("History, 1,234 events", the full number, with countLabel after it), so it is never read as a separate stop. The badge keeps its own fill and text pair on the selected, hovered and pressed tab, so its contrast does not depend on the tab behind it; its tone is never the only signal, since the number and its label say it.

### Tag

[tag.json](tag.json): A label the user applied and can remove: a chip with an optional categorical colour swatch and a remove button; TagGroup wraps them in a row.

Usage: Use Tag for labels a user adds and removes (a saved query's labels, applied filters). onRemove adds a remove button; swatch (1 to 8) adds a colour dot from the colour-blind-safe chart.cat roles so tags of different categories can be told apart. Put tags in a TagGroup (role="list") with role="listitem" on each. For a read-only status word use Badge; for choosing several values in a field use MultiSelect, which has its own chips.

- Wraps: @base-ui/react/use-render
- Parts: TagGroup (data-slot tag-group): Tags in a wrapping row, role="list".
- variant: neutral, accent, warning
- size: sm, md
- Props: children (ReactNode); variant ("neutral" | "accent" | "warning", default "neutral"); size ("sm" | "md", default "sm"); swatch (1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8); onRemove (() => void); removeLabel (string); disabled (boolean, default false); render (ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)); className (string); ref (Ref<HTMLElement>)
- States: hover (hover), focus-visible (focus-visible), disabled (data-disabled)
- Tokens: chart.cat.1, chart.cat.2, chart.cat.3, chart.cat.4, chart.cat.5, chart.cat.6, chart.cat.7, chart.cat.8, color.accent.subtle-bg, color.accent.subtle-fg, color.border.default, color.fg.default, color.fg.muted, color.interactive.hover, color.neutral.subtle-bg, color.neutral.subtle-fg, color.ring, color.ring-inner, color.status.warning.bg, color.status.warning.border, color.status.warning.fg, font.sans, opacity.disabled, radius.sm, ring.inner-width, ring.width, size.control.sm, size.control.xs, size.icon.xs, space.inline.md, space.inline.sm, space.inline.xs, text.caption.leading, text.caption.size, text.caption.tracking, text.caption.weight, text.label.leading, text.label.size, text.label.tracking, text.label.weight
- Accessibility: The label is text; the remove button is a native <button> named "Remove <label>" (or removeLabel) in the tab order. TagGroup is role="list"; give each Tag role="listitem" so screen readers count them. The swatch is aria-hidden and the chart.cat palette is colour-blind safe; the label always carries the meaning. When removing a tag moves focus, move it to the next tag's remove button or the group's input; the app owns that.

### Terminal

[terminal.json](terminal.json): An interactive terminal on xterm.js 6, loaded lazily from the app's own bundle (no CDN), themed from the terminal.* roles of its region and rethemed when they change; keystrokes leave as bytes through onData, size changes through onResize, output goes in through ref.write.

Usage: Use Terminal for an exec session or a shell: pass onData to the process's stdin (bytes, UTF-8), onResize to the process's terminal size, and write its stdout and stderr with ref.write(bytes) as they arrive (writes before xterm.js has loaded are queued). onReady fires once it is open. Set readOnly when the session ends (keystrokes are ignored, the cursor stops blinking) and ref.reset() before a new one. Mod+Shift+C copies the selection and Mod+Shift+V pastes; Ctrl+C goes to the process. ref.findNext and findPrevious search the scrollback. The height comes from className; the terminal fits its columns and rows to the element. Use LogViewer for output alone, CodeBlock for a fixed snippet.

- Wraps: no Base UI part
- Props: ref (Ref<TerminalHandle>); onData ((data: Uint8Array) => void); onResize ((cols: number, rows: number) => void); onReady (() => void); fontSize (number); scrollback (number, default 5000); readOnly (boolean, default false); screenReaderMode (boolean, default false); aria-label (string, default "Terminal"); className (string)
- States: focus-within (focus-within), loading (data-loading)
- Tokens: color.border.subtle, color.fg.muted, color.ring, font.mono, radius.lg, ring.inner-width, ring.width, space.inset.sm, terminal.bg, terminal.fg, text.code.leading, text.code.size, text.code.tracking, text.code.weight
- Accessibility: The frame is role="group" with the accessible name, which xterm.js's input (a textarea) also takes; it is the tab stop, and every key, Tab and Escape included, goes to the process. Mod+Shift+C and Mod+Shift+V copy and paste. screenReaderMode gives xterm.js's accessible buffer of the output (off by default: it costs speed); the app should also say when a session starts and ends outside the terminal. Every ANSI colour reads at 4.5:1 on terminal.bg and the cursor at 3:1 (the token build checks each pair). The frame shows the ring while the keyboard is inside: ring.width in color.ring.

### Textarea

[textarea.json](textarea.json): A multi-line text input on Base UI's Input rendering a <textarea>, in Input's appearances and sizes, with placeholder, invalid and disabled states; works inside a Field.

Usage: Use Textarea for text that may span lines (descriptions, notes, filters, short SQL); use Input for one line and the SQL editor for real queries. Appearance outline is the default; underline for dense or inline forms, filled-darker on white surfaces, filled-lighter on grey ones. The old sizes sm/md/lg still work for one release.

- States: focus-visible (focus-visible), invalid (aria-invalid), invalid-in-field (data-invalid), disabled (data-disabled)
